"Sour" crude is very low quality crude. It has a high sulfur content. When refined, the sulphur must be removed and disposed of in an environmentally safe manner which is expensive and an added cost relative to sweet crude.

The article notes that more 'sweet' crude has become available with the development of the Bakken Shale.

Would you buy an inferior product when higher quality products are available? This is probably not a temporary price inversion. The abundance of Bakken crude is squeezing out the pour quality sour crude. It makes no sense to develop or even continue extract the sour crude. The sour crude still being produced is most likely being produced under contract. As these contracts expire they will not be renewed. Indeed as the price continues to fall, many will be bought out. This is economics in action -- and an example of the beauty of the 'market' system. Price signals allocate resources to the highest value product.

FWIW: Yes, people actually 'taste' and 'smell' crude oil to see if it is 'sweet' or 'sour'. A given field varies over time, usually marginally and the quality of the crude tends to deteriorate as the field is consumed.

This is something I learned in sales.

Our body language is tied into our instincts as animals, and our legs and feet are very responsive to our subconscious as a result. They're the part of our body that we'd use to get away from dangerous or unpleasant situations.

If you're talking to someone(such as a customer or girl or whoever) and they are interested in the conversation, they will usually have both feet pointed toward you. If they are uninterested and/or uncomfortable, they will have one foot pointed away in whatever direction they would like to escape. If they cross their legs, it indicates that they are feeling comfortable or safe (because they are making it more difficult to make a sudden escape.) If they are nervous(either positive or negative nervousness), they are going to have a harder time keeping their lower body and feet still(because their instincts are telling them to leave whatever situation is making them uncomfortable.)
